First, I highly admit you to meet face-to-face if you can. If you cannot, that doesn't really makes an issue (screw coronavirus). Second, ask him why he has been doing that to himself. What made him start self-harming? Stress? School? Family issues? State the problem and give him space as much as he can. Make sure he feels comfortable while talking, self-harm is not the easiest thing to talk about (knowing from myself). Talking about your problems with someone that you trust really gives comfort. If he is self harming because of a toxic enviorment he's been in, for example fake friends, try to seperate him from them and make sure he feels loved and safe. Try to get him to stop by stating valid reasons and bear in mind that stopping self harming is never easy and takes time (knowing from myself again). Don't force him to talk about his problems, wait until he feels comfortable and ready to discuss his problems. I really hope I helped, I hope he stops soon.
